payload.title: Moment method validated for spacecraft smoke characterization
payload.finding: Combining SAMER flight and post-flight ground tests, the report concludes that the moment method with a lognormal particle-size assumption is a valid, effective way to characterize aerosol encountered in space vehicles; particle size distributions were identified for five materials common in spacecraft.
payload.proposed_relevance: Supports smoke-detector design that relies on particle-size moments; detector performance itself is not evaluated here.

payload.title: Heating temperature preferred over Rt/R0 to characterize tests
payload.finding: The report states that tests with the same Rt/R0 can have quite different sample heating temperatures, so its revised data reduction characterizes each test by heating temperature derived from engineering data instead of Rt/R0.
payload.proposed_relevance: Explains why this dashboard does not interpret Rt/R0 as a physical condition.

payload.title: Most smoke particles 200–400 nm
payload.finding: SAME-2 heated five spacecraft-representative materials (Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber, Pyrell) below their ignition point, with flow past the sample from quiescent to 8 cm/s and smoke aging from 11 to 1800 s. Most average particle sizes were 200–400 nm; some quiescent cases produced substantially larger particles.
payload.proposed_relevance: Relevant to sizing assumptions for spacecraft smoke detection; no flaming combustion occurred in these tests.

payload.title: Ambient O2 added as a controlled test variable
payload.finding: BASS-II used nitrogen dilution of the glovebox working volume for the first time on ISS, using a stirred-reactor model calibrated against onboard sensors; main variables were ambient O2, ventilation flow velocity, and fuel type, thickness and geometry.
payload.proposed_relevance: Method precedent for reduced-O2 flammability testing in orbit.

payload.title: Small heat release; fuel-rich global burning
payload.finding: Heat release rates estimated from O2 consumption and burn time (13.1 kJ per g O2) were mostly well below 100 W, and the global equivalence ratio was estimated as fuel rich, about 1.3 on average.
payload.proposed_relevance: Indicates scale of fire signatures in small orbital tests; not a material-acceptance result.

payload.title: Gas readings consistent with one-step stoichiometry
payload.finding: Before/after O2 and CO2 readings compared well with stoichiometric ratios for a one-step gas-phase reaction; CO versus CO2 followed a linear trend for some datasets but not for all fuel geometries and flows.
payload.proposed_relevance: Suggests O2/CO2 sensors can track combustion completeness; CO behaviour is configuration dependent.

payload.title: Extinction flow velocity, thin PMMA, 21% O2
payload.finding: Table 2.1 lists an experimental extinction velocity of 10 ± 5 mm/s for thin PMMA at 1 atm and 21% O2 (computation 15, theory 7.5 mm/s).
payload.proposed_relevance: Low-flow extinction limits inform ventilation-shutdown suppression strategies (proposal).

payload.title: Extinction flow velocity, thin PMMA, 16% O2
payload.finding: Table 2.1 lists an experimental extinction velocity of 30 ± 5 mm/s for thin PMMA at 1 atm and 16% O2 (computation 35, theory 10 mm/s).
payload.proposed_relevance: Low-flow extinction limits inform ventilation-shutdown suppression strategies (proposal).

payload.title: Coflow and burner size shift smoke points
payload.finding: SPICE found 52 smoke points (ethylene, propane, propylene, propylene/N2) with burners of 0.41, 0.76 and 1.6 mm and coflow 5.4–65 cm/s. Higher coflow shortened luminous flames but moved smoke points to higher fuel flow and longer flames; smaller burners had longer smoke points.
payload.proposed_relevance: Microgravity sooting data can test soot models also used for terrestrial flames (proposal).

payload.title: High microgravity sooting propensity for propane
payload.finding: Pseudo threshold-soot-index estimates from the measured smoke points indicate an unusually high sooting propensity for propane in microgravity diffusion flames.
payload.proposed_relevance: Fuel-dependent soot behaviour matters for smoke/radiation hazards; cross-gravity transfer is not established.

payload.title: Cool-flame droplet data for low-temperature chemistry
payload.finding: CFI produced cool-flame burning data for n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures and farnesane, studying pressure and helium dilution; the report states these data help validate low-temperature kinetic mechanisms relevant to low-temperature engine concepts such as HCCI.
payload.proposed_relevance: Benefit statements are the source authors' claims; no engine result is reported.

payload.title: Limiting oxygen index slightly lower than expected
payload.finding: FLEX burned methanol and n-heptane droplets (2–5 mm) at 0.70–3.05 atm with N2/CO2 dilution; observed limiting oxygen index values appeared slightly lower than initially expected, with radiative extinction at higher dilution and diffusive extinction at lower dilution.
payload.proposed_relevance: Relevant to diluent-based fire suppression and atmosphere selection; values are fuel- and geometry-specific.
